::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

This section is adapted from @zhou2024matinv and @zhou2024ls,
used under the MIT License
(see the license text in @sec-subspaces).
The first source states that every invertible matrix has an LU factorization;
that is false without reordering rows (the $2 \times 2$ row swap $\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ has none),
so this section states only how an LU factorization, when one exists, solves a system.
The least squares results are proved here from the closest-point theorem (@thm-closest-point)
rather than by differentiating, and the QR factorization is derived from Gram-Schmidt (@thm-gram-schmidt).

:::
